title: Specify the work and the team
learning_outcome: Describe requirements, roles, ownership, and failure handoffs.
exercise: Draft a short PRD and assign each step to a named role and human owner.

scenes.narration_exact: “Morgan receives a polished Session Option Brief. It compares three notes and says the facilitator is confirmed. That one word is wrong. The source said ‘available for review.’ The preparation role did what an old brief told it to do: ‘Summarize the best session option.’ That sentence left the hardest part in Morgan's head. What counts as ready? Which source is required? When must the work stop? A human colleague might ask. A paper agent design needs those answers written down.”

scenes.narration_exact: “Chapter Eleven turns the request into an Agentic PRD Packet. Seven fields carry the load: outcome, scope fences, input manifest, acceptance tests, escalation, owner, and reversal. The outcome is a comparison Morgan can review, not a session announcement. Scope fences keep the role away from participant messages and calendar changes. The input manifest lists the three Harbor note references and their freshness checks. An acceptance test says staffing language must match the facilitator note exactly in meaning. If the note is missing or ambiguous, the escalation is a hold for Morgan.”

scenes.narration_exact: “Reversal is modest here. Morgan can return a draft for correction or withdraw it from review. There is no external send to reverse. A test result belongs beside the draft as evidence: source IDs checked, staffing wording checked, review gate present. A failed check does not become a footnote under a confident recommendation. It blocks the handoff. This packet remains a proposed design; writing it does not configure an agent.”

scenes.narration_exact: “Now give the work an organization. One role checks sources; one role assembles the comparison; Morgan owns the outcome. If both preparation roles produce separate answers without a common handoff, Morgan gets a small swarm and two versions of the truth. Chapter Twelve's Pod Model asks for a charter, lead, specialists, board, standup, and handoff. For this tiny classroom pod, keep the lead as a preparation coordinator, not an approver. The board is a proposed paper status list. The standup is a short proposed summary of ready and blocked work.”

scenes.narration_exact: “The charter is narrow: prepare one evidence-bound option brief for Morgan. The source checker may flag staleness, not repair a source by inventing a newer date. The drafter may compare, not confirm staffing. The coordinator may route a blocked packet to Morgan, not override the block. The board should show who holds the next move. If nobody owns a failed source check, the org chart is decorative. Write that ownership into the handoff now.”

scenes.narration_exact: “Draft the seven-field PRD in under a page. Give it two acceptance tests, including the staffing claim, and one explicit failure route. Then sketch the Pod Model: charter, lead, specialists, board, standup, handoff, and human owner. Use role labels and course references. Use a fictional or approved example. Do not use private operational data, configure production agents, or promote the pod's coordinator into final decision authority.”
